summary: The culture adaptor is granted read verbs and the other tiers' inputs, and a scope-keyed home-room grant resolves at all.
reason: Internal only, and inert in every default deployment: [culture] enabled ships false, so nothing runs, and nothing reads what it writes (design/culture-tier 02-measurement step 4 is writing-only). Three parts. (1) The wiring defect: RegistryToolSource.build resolved every home room through home_rooms[workspace or ""] while DreamerRuntime.run supplies workspace=None for a scope-keyed adaptor, so a scope-keyed grant looked up home_rooms[""], took the loud closed branch, and every room-scoped verb answered unavailable while the grant read as honoured. A scope-keyed adaptor's key IS a conversation, so its room is an identity rather than a choice and now resolves through a new scope_rooms map built off the same allowlist. An adaptor with no grant still gets the closed, empty-room shape. (2) The culture adaptor now holds nine read verbs (ask_memory, search_memory, about, lookup_person, group_members, where_been, online_now, web_search, web_fetch), all inside the read-only ceiling and none of them an act verb, plus the room's standing position, the note index and the operator's room description as rendered inputs. where_been was in no adaptor's grant at all before this. (3) The account cap fell from 8,000 to 1,600 characters, derived against the output budgets that must emit it rather than chosen beside them: at 8,000 an account written to the cap could not be emitted, and a truncated fold holds its watermark and re-reads the same batch forever.
